message:
Sam, Theo and Priya, rigid wheels with traction bars stay afloat on loose soil without tracks.

Flotation stays shallow because weight spreads wide. The Black Point 1 (BP-1) friction source E1 shows high friction near 39 to 51 degrees with negligible cohesion and the density source E2 shows bulk density near 1.6 to 1.9 grams per cubic centimetre, while the ground-pressure calc evidence E10 gives about 9.82 kilopascal, like a person standing on soft snow, so large 300 millimetre diameter wheels avoid the mass and height cost of tracks.

Sam, Theo and Priya, front transverse drum meaning rotating cutter takes a shallow steady bite with low pull.

Cutting stays small against weight for traction. The cutting source E4 and cutting source E5 average near 39 newton and the excavator source E6 describes counter-rotating drums, while the pull-ratio calc evidence E12 gives 0.066 against about 589 newton weight from the weight calc evidence E9, like lifting a 4 kilogram bag, so a 30 millimetre cut holds margin if the load stays centred.

Sam, Theo and Priya, deeper cut would raise drive current and forward moment, linking my traction to your power and tip. I am not ready while blocking objection O2 on lift tip and stowed fit stays open, and I condition support for integration on closure of mass and dump proofs owned by others.
